55+ homes you can buy in Coquitlam

Coquitlam's 55+ ownership sits in one pocket: three strata buildings around the Town Centre on Guildford Way, Princess Crescent and Burlington Drive, plus one manufactured-home park on Dewdney Trunk Road in Ranch Park. Each row says what you own and how the 55+ rule is evidenced.

blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around Coquitlam

items.t: The 55+ strata cluster sits in the Town Centre / City Centre pocket that board sources label North Coquitlam and Canyon Springs.
Schools: School District 43 (Coquitlam), address-based catchments through the SD43 School Locator.
Libraries: Coquitlam Public Library City Centre branch, 1169 Pinetree Way, and Poirier branch, 575 Poirier Street, plus the Library Link mobile service.

Where the 55+ stock actually sits: (1) ownership — one pocket only, the Town Centre (Guildford Way, Princess Crescent, Burlington Drive) plus one manufactured-home park in Ranch Park (Dewdney Trunk Road); (2) retirement/care — Dufferin Street in the centre and the Maillardville cluster in the south/west; (3) subsidized rental — split by BC Housing into "North" (Johnson St / Pipeline Rd / Ozada Ave) and "South" (Burquitlam / Maillardville). Burke Mountain, Cape Horn, Eagle Ridge, Chineside and Harbour Chines each returned zero known 55+ stock of any tenure.

items.t: North list: Friendship Manor / Friendship Place (1150–1160 Johnson St); Ozada Village (1205 Pipeline Rd); Robert Nicklin Place (3100 Ozada Ave — mixed affordable rental, not 55+-only).

South list (Burquitlam): Cottonwood (515 Cottonwood Ave, BC Housing managed); Dogwood (710 Dogwood St, BC Housing managed — not to be confused with Port Coquitlam's Dogwood Manor / Dogwood Place on Seymour St, a different city).

South list (Maillardville): Chateau De Ville (1111 Brunette Ave); Le Chateau Place (312 Schoolhouse St); Mountain View Suites (1110 King Albert Ave) — all non-profit entries in the Coquitlam — South list.

blocks.text: Looks like a Coquitlam 55+ building but is not

items.t: The Burlington — 2968 / 2978 Burlington Drive: The near-namesake across from Burlington Estates: strata plan LMS923, 128 units, built 1993, freehold strata, pets allowed with restrictions.

Wildwood Park — 201 Cayer St (Maillardville): not a 55+ park: listings describe a "family-oriented neighbourhood" with a pool, tennis court, clubhouse and a playground, homes leasehold non-strata on rented pads. Its appearance in 55+ searches is a search artefact from grouping with the genuinely 55+ Hideaway Park.
Mill Creek Village — 145 King Edward St (Maillardville): The city's other manufactured-home park: listings describe a "well managed family friendly manufactured home park." Family park.

55One — 551 Emerson St (Burquitlam): A 308-suite purpose-built rental tower with 100 provincially funded affordable homes for families, seniors and people living with disabilities mixed through the tower, operated by 43 Housing Society. Despite the name, it is not a 55+ building — the "55" is the street number (551 Emerson).

Robert Nicklin Place — 3100 Ozada Ave: A six-storey, 164-unit affordable rental building by Lincoln Station, operated by Affordable Housing Societies: tenant priority covers families with low incomes as well as seniors and people with disabilities. Mixed affordable rental, not 55+ — and not on Burke Mountain despite the riding name.
2960 Princess Crescent and the other Princess Crescent buildings beside Princess Gate: only the Princess Gate addresses (2985 / 2995) are known 55+. Check the civic address, not the street name.

blocks.text: Local rules and plans in Coquitlam
BC’s 55+ rules (age bylaws, who may live in a unit, exemptions and rentals) apply in every strata and are on the BC 55+ strata rules page.
Good to know about 55+ homes in Coquitlam

items.t: BC Housing's map will mislead a Coquitlam search in both directions: Anyone building a sub-area seniors list straight from that directory will import buildings that do not belong there.

Two Dogwoods, two cities: Coquitlam's subsidized list includes Dogwood at 710 Dogwood St (Burquitlam, BC Housing managed); Port Coquitlam's subsidized seniors buildings are Dogwood Manor (3155 Seymour St) and Dogwood Place (3125 Seymour St). Similar names, different cities, different operators — confirm the city before applying.

blocks.source: Source: MLS® data from the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® and the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board, compiled by SnapStats®. Sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed. On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal. Condos and townhomes are one line in the reports.

faq.q: Is Coquitlam a buyers’ or sellers’ market?
faq.a: In October 2026 houses in Coquitlam had a sales ratio of 14%, which the reports’ scale reads as a balanced market, and condos and townhomes 16%, which the reports’ scale reads as a balanced market. On the reports’ scale under 12% favours buyers, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% favours sellers.

faq.q: How many 55+ homes are for sale in Coquitlam?
faq.a: The listing feed on this page shows what is active now, and the number changes daily. Ask Jared and he will send you the 55+ homes in Coquitlam that match what you want.

faq.q: Do these numbers separate condos from townhomes?
faq.a: The monthly SnapStats reports publish condos and townhomes as one line, so the monthly counts here include both. The boards’ benchmark prices are published separately for apartments and townhomes.

faq.q: What 55+ homes can I actually buy in Coquitlam?
faq.a: Three strata buildings, all in the Town Centre pocket — Marlborough House (3098 Guildford Way), Princess Gate (2985 / 2995 Princess Crescent) and Burlington Estates (2963 / 2973 Burlington Drive) — plus manufactured homes on rented pads at Hideaway Park (4200 Dewdney Trunk Rd, Ranch Park). No known 55+ strata exists anywhere else in the city.

faq.q: If I need help later, can I stay in Coquitlam?
faq.a: The in-city ladder is: independent 55+ strata living in the Town Centre buildings; retirement-residence rental at Venvi Parkwood Manor (1142 Dufferin St) and assisted living at Residences at Belvedere (750 Delestre Ave, 60 funded suites by referral); then long-term care at Dufferin Care Centre (1131 Dufferin St), Foyer Maillard (1010 Alderson Ave, 125 beds) and Cartier House (1419 Cartier Ave) through the health-authority process. Two further 55+ affordable rental buildings (S.U.C.C.E.S.S., 158 homes total) are under construction.
